blind.why: FP Arc burst at 12m in a live match (b/f04) vs CS2 t1_019. Ours reads the hit clearly: crystal-white target, pink mist and hit X. But the hard 8-point starburst flash and the full-length tracer look pasted onto the frame. CS2's soft fireball and small puff sit in the world, so it looks more polished and cohesive.

Hit on a distant enemy with tracer (i/fp00) vs CS2 t2_029. CS2's large mist and single soft tracer make the hit obvious. Ours shows a thick saturated pink beam from a teammate behind the camera that runs right into the target, plus small hit rings and stray grey floor puffs. The tracer is louder than the hit.

Tag-out moment at 12m (b/f16) vs CS2 kill aftermath t2_008. Our confetti is pretty in a crop, but at full frame it is a fist-sized cluster of 2-4px flecks plus a faint floor ring, and it leaves nothing behind. CS2's lasting wall and floor splatter makes the kill spot readable for seconds.

Rifle fire at a wall (p/fp_auto_1) vs CS2 t4_026. The wall impact now sits on the crosshair and is readable, which is good, but its white core blob covers the crosshair centre. Together with the starburst, the frame is busier than CS2's tight flash and ejected casing.

biggest_gap: Other actors' tracers are too loud and clutter the duel. Repro: ?test=1&seed=1&match=1&phase=live. Put the local player at ember spawn 0 facing an enemy 12-15m away; teammates spawn behind you (shots/critic-vfx/b/f06, b/f08, i/fp00, i_crop.png). Each teammate shot draws a 5-10px saturated pink beam with glow from the screen edge or bottom-left all the way into the enemy you are aiming at, and it stays up for several frames. It is the brightest thing on screen besides the flash, and it lies over the target silhouette. CS2 tracers are thin (1-3px), short (about 1-2m) segments that travel fast and fade, and are drawn only on some shots. Fix for tracers not fired by the local player: draw a moving 1.5-3m segment, not the whole from-to line; use about 40-60% width and alpha for tracers that start behind or beside the camera; and fade the segment out within about 1.5m of any enemy the viewer is aiming at, or at the hit point.
other_gaps: Bullet-hole decals over-corrected. Each one is now a soft-edged dark blob about 9cm across (about 15px at 4m, 1280x720), and every one looks the same. A spray looks like a column of soot or paintball smudges (shots/critic-vfx/crop_decal.png), not crisp small holes. Make them about 3-4cm with a sharp dark core and a thin, lighter chipped ring tinted by the surface, and vary rotation, size and shape.

Tag-out at range is too small to sell the 'glass shatter' moment. At 12m the confetti is 2-4px flecks in about 1.5m (b/f16-f18), and nothing persists afterwards. Scale fleck size with distance, which bodySpark already does, add a single bright crystal flash or burst frame, and leave a short-lived (5-10s) glitter or scorch mark on the floor where the player went down.

Impact/hit rings: white 'o' rings and glow cores linger about 100ms next to the enemy (i_crop.png, frames 5-7, on the crate beside the target) and on the crosshair (pair4). In fights they compete with the enemy silhouette. Make them shorter (about 50ms), dimmer, and tinted by the surface rather than white.

Hard-landing shock ring (lab land-hard): a white disc expands to about 2-3m radius. It reads like the Pulse utility, and bunny-hopping enemies will scatter these across the floor. Keep landing to dust only, and use a ring only for jump pads.

Cross-piece (not vfx-owned, verified by hiding the vfx group): the viewmodel FP flash is still a hard 8-point star visible for 3 frames (about 50ms), with a large white smoke glow at the muzzle 0.2-0.4s after the last shot (b/f14-f15). Cosmetics additive Points draw yellow glowing bokeh dots around the local player's feet at the bottom of the screen (shots/critic-vfx/crop_blobs.png).
strengths: No console errors. vfx.update costs about 0.1ms max in a live fight, and vfx adds only about 10-17 draw calls during a firefight.
Body-hit feedback now carries at 12m: the target flashes crystal-white with tagger-pink mist on the hit frame.
The local wall impact sits on the crosshair and is clearly readable during auto fire, and the FP flash no longer blocks the aim point.
The confetti shatter, seen up close, is crisp, on palette, and has a nice spin and fall.
